name: pqsigner-fv-adversarial-review
doc: Machine-readable protocol for the PQSigner FV adversarial review. Framework-AGNOSTIC: run_review.py drives ANY backend (Claude Code, Codex, a raw LLM, a future agent) that can read a prompt and emit JSON. The reviewer persona + the green-but-hollow catalog live in PROMPT.md; this file defines WHAT to review (angles + targets), HOW MANY independent passes (reviewers) and the agreement rule (quorum), and the STRICT output schema every backend must satisfy. See docs/verification/fv-adversarial-review-playbook.md for the full method and README.md to run it.

defaults.comment: reviewers = independent passes per angle (cross-vote); quorum = passes that must agree for a finding to be 'confirmed'. Defaults are rate-limit-gentle (2 passes, serial). For a stronger adversarial pass use reviewers=3 quorum=2 (majority). jobs>1 parallelises but can trip provider rate limits.

root_doc: Repo root, relative to this protocol file. Target globs below resolve from here so the review can span firmware (secure/, fsbl/) AND proofs (contracts/verification/).

angles.title: Lean proof vacuity (V1-V4, V6, V10)
angles.instructions: Hunt green-but-hollow LEAN proofs. For each theorem in scope, separate the CLAIM (what the name/comment advertises) from the GUARANTEE (what the statement actually establishes). Look for: vacuous antecedents (a hypothesis no input satisfies -> the theorem is about nothing); dead conjuncts / unused hypotheses (deleting them changes nothing); `: True`-typed or `trivial`-closed statements dressed as content; conclusions weaker than the name implies; stub `def`s the theorem quantifies over (noncomputable placeholder signers/oracles); and `#print axioms`-bypass via native_decide/reduceBool/@[implemented_by]. For every candidate, name a PoC: the mutation that SHOULD break it but would not, or the input the antecedent can never take. The proof-mutation gate (scripts/check_proof_mutations.py) and lint_fv_invariants.sh exist — assume they run; find what they MISS.

angles.title: Ledger advertised-vs-actual (V5, V7)
angles.instructions: Compare the human-facing assurance claims against the machine truth. Read AXIOM_STATUS.json (status, closures, signature_pins, summary counts), THE_CLAIM.md, THREE_CLAIMS_PROOF.md, ASSURANCE_CASE.md, README assurance lines. For each advertised 'discharged'/'proven'/'kernel-checked' claim, ask: does the cited artifact ACTUALLY establish it, or a weaker/adjacent thing? Look for: a status of 'discharged' over a hypothesis still carried raw (the P1/hInv class); an axiom advertised as a 'marker' that is actually load-bearing (or vice-versa); a closure claim that omits an axiom the dump shows; counts that drift from the array; a codehash pin that is stale; a 'fully proven to bytecode' that is really KAT+mutant testing. PoC = the exact divergence (ledger says X, dump/source says Y).

angles.title: Model != deployed artifact (V8, V9, V11)
angles.instructions: Attack the bridge between the verified MODEL and the real ARTIFACT. The proofs are over Lean models / Halmos transcriptions / extracted Lean; the guarantees only transfer if those faithfully mirror the deployed bytecode, the shipped Rust firmware, and the wire formats. Look for: a Lean model that accepts inputs the bytecode rejects (or vice-versa); a Halmos 'pointwise equivalence' against a hand-written LeanModel.sol that itself diverges from the contract; a wrong-quantifier proof (claims forall, proves it for representatives / concrete keys only — the A3.2 unset-index ceiling, the A3.1 forall-signature ceiling); an extracted-Lean function that drifted from the Rust it was extracted from; a domain-tag / digest preimage in Lean that differs from proto/the device. PoC = a concrete input where model and artifact disagree, or the precise quantifier gap.

angles.title: Crypto reduction soundness (V7, V2)
angles.instructions: Attack the cryptographic axioms for LATENT FALSITY and inconsistency — the class mutation testing canNOT catch (a false axiom still type-checks while lean/ is mathlib-free). Read Crypto/Assumptions.lean, EUFCMA.lean, the EUF_CMA_INCONSISTENCY.md history, the BreaksHash firewall. Look for: an axiom that is mathematically FALSE as stated (the sha256_injective-on-fixed-length class — pigeonhole-false, non-detonatable only because no mathlib); a reduction that can conclude False / lets `¬ BreaksHash` be derived (re-detonating the EUF-CMA inconsistency); a 'shape' axiom that is secretly `True`; a conjunct that is non-operational (isForgery unsatisfiable for any real message). PoC = the falsifying witness (the collision, the empty-transcript forgery) or the inconsistency derivation.

angles.title: Firmware FI / control-flow gates (F1-F16 surface)
angles.instructions: Attack the FIRMWARE security gates the EF firmware findings targeted. Read the FI-hardened sign paths, the rollback/counter logic, the FW-update verify chain, the offchain counter store. Look for: an outer verify gate the optimiser can fold (missing black_box / volatile); a sentinel/CFI counter that is checked but not consumed; a fail-OPEN default where fail-closed is required; a counter that can be replayed or skipped; a 'voted max(a,b)' that should fail-closed-on-disagreement (or vice-versa); a digest preimage that omits a field. PoC = the fault/input/ordering that bypasses the gate. NOTE: firmware is not Lean-proven; the bar is a concrete bypass, not a proof gap.

angles.title: Firmware Kani harness vacuity + scope (V1/V3/V6/V8/V11 + G3) -- the FIRST non-Lean surface profile; model new surfaces on this
angles.instructions: Hunt VACUOUS or SCOPE-LIMITED firmware Kani proofs -- the ~76 #[kani::proof] harnesses (in #[cfg(kani)] mod verification blocks) gating the clear-sign decoders + counters + the FW-update manifest. The mechanical gate (scripts/check_kani_mutations.py + kani_mutations.json, `make verify-kani-mutation`) already screens for a load-bearing mutation a harness fails to catch -- ASSUME it runs; find what it structurally CANNOT: (V1) a kani::assume(...) so tight it empties the input space (assume(false), or a precondition no real companion input satisfies) so the harness proves nothing; (V3) a #[kani::proof] with no assertion, or asserting a tautology / a definitional identity; (V6) a decoder verified against a re-implementation of ITSELF (a self-derived oracle, not an independent reference); (V8 -- THE BIG ONE) a BOUNDED proof presented as universal: #[kani::unwind(N)] / a fixed [u8; N] symbolic buffer / kani::any::<[u8;N]>() where the comment or ledger implies for-all but only <=N records / <=N bytes are covered (multiSend is bounded to <=2 records at N=180) -- ask whether the caller's cap actually makes the bound sound, or whether an adversary payload past N is simply unproven; (V11 -- THE OTHER BIG ONE) a harness proving 'no panic / no OOB / canonical accept' when the WYSIWYS threat is 'the RENDER matches the calldata' -- the renderer is #[cfg(not(test))] and OUT of Kani's reach, so gate==renderer rests on by-construction + host tests, NOT the Kani proof; attack any implication that a decode-decision proof secures the DISPLAY. Also G3 (coverage): which decoders / sign-paths / counter-transitions have NO harness at all? Cross-reference contracts/verification/docs/FV_SURFACE_MAP.md -- this firmware-Kani surface has never had a first adversarial pass. PoC per finding: the concrete input past the bound (V8), a load-bearing mutation kani_mutations.json omits (V1/V6), or the wrong-property gap (V11). Tag v_class V1/V3/V6/V8/V11 or G3.

backends.claude: cat {prompt_file} | claude -p --output-format text --allowedTools Read Grep Glob

backends_doc: A backend is any shell command that reads the assembled prompt (the {prompt_file} placeholder is replaced with a temp file path) and writes the model's JSON answer to stdout. claude/codex are AGENTS with file-read tools, so the prompt lists target paths and they read them — the templates MUST grant read access or the agent denies/hangs in non-interactive mode: `claude -p` needs `--allowedTools Read Grep Glob`; `codex exec` needs `--sandbox read-only` (lets the model read files, blocks writes). These templates match backends/claude.sh + backends/codex.sh exactly (keep them in sync). For a tool-less backend (raw API), pass --inline-files so file contents are embedded in the prompt. The 'generic' backend takes --cmd verbatim (use it for self-test: --backend generic --cmd 'cat tests/canned_findings.json'). The model's JSON answer may be surrounded by reasoning/tool logs on stdout; run_review.py brace-scans for the last balanced {findings:...} object.

id.doc: short kebab slug, unique within this answer

v_class.doc: V1..V11 (see PROMPT.md), or 'FW' for a firmware bypass, or 'NA'

defect.doc: why the guarantee is hollow/false/weaker than the claim

poc.doc: MANDATORY: the concrete reproduction (mutation that should break it but does not; input the predicate should reject but accepts; the falsifying witness; the bypass ordering). If you could NOT produce one, write 'NONE' and set severity to low/info.

honest_residual.doc: MANDATORY eliminative-argumentation field: what you could NOT verify, what you assumed true, which targets you did not fully read, and where your own findings might be wrong. A review that claims to have found everything is itself a V-class failure.
